title: Judgement mirrors the deed, image for image

points.label: What research comes close
points.text: **Sayyid Qutb** sees the punishment here as “of the same nature as the deed”: wood, rope, fire and lahab. Even the sound enacts the scene. Surah 78:26 names the idea: **jazāʾan wifāqan**, “a fitting recompense”.
points.who: Sayyid Qutb, In the Shade of the Qur’an

points.label: One possible reading
points.text: Nothing is brought in from outside: his **name**, her **load** and the **rope** of her work become the sentence. Judgement is pictured less as a penalty imposed than as **deeds coming home**, a life turned back on the one who lived it.

bottom_text: This is one reading. “Abu Lahab” was a nickname for his glowing face, given before the surah; and exegetes split on whether firewood and rope are her deeds now or hell’s torment.
source_label: Sayyid Qutb, In the Shade of the Qur’an, Surah 111 · Zaheer, Ishraq al-Ma‘ani
